notes:
Executive summary: Northbridge Media Labs was evaluating Redwood Dedicated/Private for real-time chat and moderation across live sports and breaking news streams. Primary concern throughout discussions: unpredictable burst traffic during live events (millisecond SLAs for top-tier customers) and the risk that queueing would degrade UX. Security/legal escalated a requirement for an air-gapped ingest pipeline for certain rights-managed feeds — Redwood Private demo did not fully address that ask. Finance instituted a hiring freeze which paused procurement; AE sensed reluctance to commit without quantifiable throughput guarantees. Competitive pressure from Anthropic + internal build option (SREs prefer controlling capacity) increased risk.

Key quotes / call snippets: "If we have even a single 10–15s token stall during halftime, advertisers will pull spend. That's non-starter." — Head of Product.

Technical notes: stress tests run on dev cluster (Mar 1 POC) hit sustained 25k concurrent streams with spikes to 120k events/min; median latency 50ms but tail percentiles spiked under synthetic burst to 1.2s when KV cache warmed poorly. SE followups outlined config changes (larger warm pools, pre-warming hooks, dedicated burst nodes) but customer lacked SRE head to approve infra tradeoffs.

Commercial notes: pricing deck shared (Drive), trial credits exhausted. Procurement asked for an SLA addendum and a capacity runbook; legal requested data residency and KMS proof. No final contract — finance froze all new infra commitments for Q1. Decision: closed-lost (Feb 15) — moved to watchlist.

Suggested re‑engage plan: 1) Provide a focused tech brief: detailed burst-capacity playbook + runbook for halftime-like events, 2) Offer a 3-month pilot with guaranteed burst nodes and penalties for missed SLOs (if legal approves), 3) Keep regular check-ins with product & infra hiring updates (90d cadence).
